rationale: The two legs multiply to (oibdp−xint)/(ME+dltt+dlc), i.e. a rank-decomposed restatement of the already-evaluated After-Interest Claim Yield (and structurally a twin of Scalable Sales Claim Value), so it is a rediscovery rather than a new mechanism.

It reuses the archived sales-to-claims value leg but swaps in an accrual-free, three-year-smoothed cash-conversion condition, which is a substantive (if incremental) change to the profitability channel and worth one test, though its implicit product is close to a plain cash-flow-to-enterprise-value yield.

This is a window-and-denominator tweak of the archived Cheap Sales Margin Upswing, whose FMB slope and long-short alpha already carried opposite signs — a symptom the proposal does not diagnose, so shortening the trend window is a cosmetic variant rather than a fix.

Both legs are near-monotone inversions of the archived Scalable Sales Claim Value's components, so the signal is largely the mirror image of an existing test and offers essentially no new information beyond a sign flip.

The expression matches the stated hypothesis and the R&D add-back is an economically motivated correction to the profitability leg, but the sales-to-price value leg and R&D intensity are each well-documented anomalies, so the incremental novelty rests entirely on the interaction.

This introduces a genuinely different value channel (payout yield) than the archive's sales/asset-based ones and is internally consistent, though quality-screened dividend yield is close to well-known practitioner strategies and the mass of zero-dividend firms will pile up at the bottom rank and degrade the short leg.
